question: Who works the most hours per year?
stat_label: Average annual hours worked per worker
source_name: Penn World Table 11 via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Indonesia leads this set. The 'siesta' stereotype doesn't survive the data: the average Greek worker puts in about 560 more hours a year than the average German.
headline: Grindset Nations

question: Who drinks the most alcohol per person?
stat_label: Total alcohol per capita (age 15+), litres of pure alcohol
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Romania tops WHO's estimates at 16.8 litres of pure alcohol per adult a year, and Uganda (11.3 L) drinks more than Italy (7.0 L). India is at 4.1 L and Turkey at 1.7 L. WHO estimates for 2020 (recorded plus unrecorded alcohol, adults 15+).
headline: Bottoms Up

question: Which country has the highest adult obesity rate?
stat_label: Adults (18+) with obesity, BMI ≥ 30 (crude estimate)
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory (via Our World in Data)
fun_fact: Egypt's adult obesity rate is slightly higher than America's in WHO's 2024 estimates. France's is less than a third of either.
headline: Heavyweights

question: Where are people happiest with their lives?
stat_label: Life satisfaction (Cantril ladder, 0–10)
source_name: World Happiness Report / Wellbeing Research Centre via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Costa Rica and Mexico both report higher life satisfaction than the US and UK, despite much lower incomes.
headline: Happy Places

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: The US homicide rate is about twice India's, and Indonesia's is lower than Finland's. Note: latest available years differ by country.
headline: Homicide Rates

question: Where are women the biggest share of STEM graduates?
stat_label: Female share of tertiary STEM graduates
source_name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Women make up a majority of STEM graduates in Algeria. In Germany, it's under 30%.
headline: Lab Coats

question: Who lives the longest?
stat_label: Life expectancy at birth
source_name: World Bank, World Development Indicators (UN Population Division)
fun_fact: Babies born in Chile and Costa Rica can expect to outlive babies born in the United States by about two years.
headline: Long Livers

question: Where do women have the most children?
stat_label: Total fertility rate (births per woman)
source_name: World Bank, World Development Indicators (UN Population Division)
fun_fact: Iran's fertility rate is now about the same as the US and France. Israel has the highest of these by far.
headline: Fertility Rate

question: Which parliament has the most women?
stat_label: Seats held by women in national parliament
source_name: Inter-Parliamentary Union via World Bank, World Development Indicators
fun_fact: Rwanda has had the world's highest share of women in parliament for years, ahead of Sweden and far ahead of the US.
headline: Madam Speaker

question: Which drivers are most likely to be in a fatal crash per mile driven?
stat_label: US passenger-vehicle driver fatal crash involvements per 100 million miles
source_name: IIHS Fatality Facts: Males and females (FARS + NHTS)
fun_fact: Per mile, male drivers overall are in 48% more fatal crashes than female drivers. Over age 70, though, women's rate is higher than men's.
headline: Fatal Crash Rates

question: Where is the female homicide rate highest?
stat_label: Intentional homicide victims, female
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators (VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5)
fun_fact: In 2022 the female homicide rate in the United States (2.81 per 100k) was higher than in India (2.37), about 3.4x the rate in Germany (0.82), 4x Jordan (0.70) and 5.6x South Korea (0.50), the lowest of these five.
headline: Female Homicide

question: Where is the homicide rate highest, by sex?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 of that sex (male or female population)
source_name: UNODC via World Bank, World Development Indicators (VC.IHR.PSRC.MA.P5 / VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5)
fun_fact: The female homicide rate in the US (2.81 per 100k) was over 3x the male rate in Germany (0.81), and 14x the male rate in Japan (0.20).
headline: Homicide by Sex

question: Where are women most likely to be in the workforce?
stat_label: Female labor force participation rate (% of women 15+, ILO modeled estimate)
source_name: ILO modeled estimates via World Bank, World Development Indicators (SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS)
fun_fact: Women in the UAE work outside the home at nearly the same rate as American women, and Saudi women now out-participate Indian women. Italy trails the UAE by 12 points.
headline: Working Women

question: Which country has the highest suicide rate?
stat_label: Age-standardized suicide rate, both sexes
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator MH_12 (Global Health Estimates)
fun_fact: Age-standardized, South Korea's rate (23.4) is still the highest of these five, but India (15.3) is above Japan (14.4) and the US (13.3), and Sweden's 'gloomy Nordic' reputation still doesn't hold: it's the lowest at 12.7. These are WHO modelled, age-standardized estimates for 2023, with wide uncertainty where death registration is weak.
headline: Suicide Rates

question: Whose lifestyle emits the most CO₂ per person?
stat_label: Consumption-based CO₂ emissions per person (emissions embedded in what a country consumes, incl. imports, minus exports)
source_name: Global Carbon Budget (Global Carbon Project) via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Counting the emissions in everything people buy, Singapore (32.3 t) is the world's #1, about twice the US (15.8 t). 'Green' Switzerland (13.3 t) is near the US because it imports most of its footprint, while China (7.6 t) and India (1.8 t) are far lower.
headline: Carbon Shoppers

question: Who emits the most CO₂ per person?
stat_label: Territorial fossil CO₂ emissions per person (fossil fuels and industry, excl. land use)
source_name: Global Carbon Budget (Global Carbon Project) via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia (20.4 t) tops this set, and the average Australian (14.5 t) now emits slightly more than the average American (14.2 t). The average person in China (8.7 t) emits nearly twice as much as the average Briton (4.5 t).
headline: Smokestacks

question: Where are 19-year-old women tallest?
stat_label: Mean height of 19-year-old girls
source_name: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC), Lancet 2020;396:1511-24
fun_fact: 19-year-old women in China (163.5 cm) are now slightly taller than in the US (163.3 cm). They've gained 6.1 cm since 1985, versus 0.4 cm in the US. UK women (163.9 cm) are just ahead. These three are within each other's uncertainty ranges, so treat it as a near-tie.
headline: Tall Girls

question: Where are 19-year-old men tallest?
stat_label: Mean height of 19-year-old boys
source_name: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC), Lancet 2020;396:1511-24
fun_fact: China's 19-year-old men (175.7 cm) gained 8.0 cm since 1985, more than any other country, and are now only 1.2 cm shorter than Americans (176.9 cm, +1.2 cm since 1985). Japan's are 172.1 cm.
headline: Tall Guys

question: In Texas, who is most likely to be convicted of a crime?
stat_label: Criminal conviction rate (all crimes), Texas, 2013–2022 average
source_name: Cato Institute, Policy Analysis No. 977 (Nowrasteh, 2024), using Texas DPS data
fun_fact: Native-born Texans had the highest conviction rate (1,321 per 100k), about twice that of undocumented immigrants (685) and legal immigrants (551). For homicide it was 3.0 vs 2.2 vs 1.2 per 100k. An independent PNAS 2020 study of Texas felony arrests found the same ordering for violent crime. Caveats: the rates are not adjusted for age or sex, and Cato itself calls the non-homicide conviction data less reliable, because immigration status is checked less often for minor crimes.
headline: Texas Convictions

question: In England & Wales, which citizens were most likely to be convicted?
stat_label: Approximate convictions per 10,000 residents aged 16+, by citizenship (non-citizens only; naturalised Britons count as UK)
source_name: Migration Observatory (Univ. of Oxford) analysis of MoJ conviction data and 2021 Census
fun_fact: British citizens (57.9 per 10k) had a higher conviction rate than Bangladeshi (52.5), Pakistani (46.8), Indian (25.7) and Chinese (13.9) nationals. Rates vary widely by nationality: Albanian nationals were highest (766), and the Migration Observatory warns that undercounted populations inflate some rates. Caveats: this counts non-citizens only (naturalised and UK-born minorities count as UK), short-stay and unauthorised migrants are missing from the denominator, and it describes citizenship groups, not ethnicity.
headline: In the Dock

question: Which pupils score highest at GCSE in England?
stat_label: Average Attainment 8 score (out of 90), state-funded schools, England
source_name: Department for Education via GOV.UK Ethnicity facts and figures
fun_fact: Chinese pupils score highest of all groups (65.5), then Indian (59.4). Bangladeshi (51.9) and Black African (48.7) pupils both outscore White British pupils (44.9), who rank 13th of 18 groups. Within every group, pupils eligible for free school meals score lower (White British FSM pupils average 30.9).
headline: Top of the Class

question: Where are child sexual-abuse sentences longest?
stat_label: Average prison sentence for sexual abuse of a child under 12 (months)
source_name: WODC report 3130 (van Koppen, Wijkman & de Wilde, VU Amsterdam, 2021), Table 36
fun_fact: In the sampled rulings, the average unsuspended sentence was 148 months in Ireland, 90 in Germany and 88 in Scotland, versus 37 in the Netherlands and 31 in Switzerland. Foreign samples are small (4–17 rulings each), so the authors urge caution. Statutory maxima also differ (10 years in Switzerland, 12 in the Netherlands, 15 in Germany, life in Ireland and Scotland), and the Dutch sample (105 rulings, 2015–19) is far larger than the foreign ones.
headline: Child Abuse Sentences

question: Which group voted most for Trump in 2024?
stat_label: Share voting for Trump, 2024 presidential election (national exit poll)
source_name: CNN national exit poll (Edison Research for the National Election Pool), final weighting
fun_fact: Latino men (54% Trump, 44% Harris) backed Trump slightly more than White women (53/46). Asian women (43/54) leaned Trump more than Asian men (38/56), and Black men were 21/77. This is an exit poll of 22,966 voters (10,818 men, 12,068 women); subgroup margins of error are several points. The Asian subgroups rest on a few hundred interviews (likely ±5–8 pts), and Latino men and White women differ by just 1 point.
headline: Trump Voters

question: Which American men most agree a woman should tend the home?
stat_label: % of men who agree women should tend home while men work
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation, weight WTSSNRPS / WTSSNRPS_AS)
fun_fact: Hispanic men (36.8%) agreed most, then Black men (33.4%); Asian (27.1%) and White (26.5%) men were about level. Caveats: Asian vs White and Black vs Asian are statistically tied, and the Asian figure comes from a small sample (295 men, about ±6 pts). Only the gaps between Hispanic and White men and between Black and White men are statistically clear. Pooled GSS 2016–2024, weighted (n: Hispanic 784, Black 700, White 3,161).
headline: Kitchen Debate

question: Who approves most of the switch from communism to a market economy?
stat_label: % approving the change to a market economy since 1989/1991, by country and age
source_name: Pew Research Center, Spring 2019 Global Attitudes Survey (European Public Opinion Three Decades After the Fall of Communism, p.23)
fun_fact: Young Bulgarians (74%) approve most, and Czechs aged 60+ who lived under communism (69%) beat young Russians (51%). Older Slovaks (49%) are about level with young Russians, and Russians 60+ (30%) are the only group here where most disapprove.
headline: Market Transition

question: Whose young men have the highest testosterone?
stat_label: Mean morning salivary testosterone, men 15–29
source_name: Ellison et al. 2002, Human Reproduction 17(12):3251-3 (Table I)
fun_fact: With one assay for everyone, young Massachusetts men had the highest salivary testosterone (335), ahead of Lese farmers in DR Congo (286), Tamang herders in Nepal (251) and Ache foragers in Paraguay (197). Samples are small (15–24 men per group), and these are specific communities, not whole countries. Salivary testosterone is a proxy for free testosterone, and the US sample was recruited by advertisement.
headline: Testosterone

question: Which American men most oppose special efforts to hire and promote women?
stat_label: % of men who oppose special efforts to hire/promote women
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation; weights WTSSNRPS, WTSSNRPS_AS for 2022/24)
fun_fact: White men (28%) were most likely to reject special efforts to hire women, then Asian (23%), Hispanic (19%) and Black men (12%). That's the reverse of the 'woman should tend the home' question, where Hispanic and Black men had the higher rates. Caveats: the Asian vs Hispanic gap isn't statistically significant, the Asian sample is small (271 men, about ±6 pts), and answers partly reflect views on affirmative action in general. Pooled GSS 2016–2024, weighted.
headline: Hiring Hang-ups

question: Which American men most oppose preferential hiring of women?
stat_label: % of men who oppose preferential hiring of women
source_name: NORC General Social Survey 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024 (own tabulation; weights WTSSNRPS, WTSSNRPS_AS for 2022/24)
fun_fact: Most men in every group but one opposed it: White 74%, Asian 62%, Hispanic 60%. Black men were the exception at 37%. Caveats: Asian and Hispanic men are statistically tied, the Asian sample is small (147 men, about ±10 pts), and answers partly reflect views on affirmative action in general. Pooled GSS 2016–2024, weighted.
headline: Preferential Hiring

question: Homicide rate: world cities. Which is highest?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 residents, 2024
source_name: Consejo Ciudadano para la Seguridad Pública y la Justicia Penal (CCSPJP, Mexico), "Ranking 2024 de las 50 ciudades más violentas del mundo"
fun_fact: Memphis (48.0) is almost level with Johannesburg (49.0) and above Colombia's Cali (42.3). Baltimore (35.6) is above Brazil's Manaus (31.2). Ranks are within CCSPJP's list of the world's 50 most violent cities (300k+ people, war zones excluded). Caveats: this is an NGO ranking (CCSPJP) that has been criticised for mixing metro areas with city limits and for uneven data. Its US counts include all homicides, so they run above FBI figures (Memphis is 40.9 in FBI data).
headline: City Homicide

question: Homicide rate: US vs the world. Which city is highest?
stat_label: Homicides per 100,000 residents, 2024 (official city/police figures; sources differ by country)
source_name: FBI Crime Data Explorer (Memphis PD, Chicago PD, 2024); SESNSP via Observatorio Interactivo de Incidencia Delictiva (Mexico City); SSP-SP (São Paulo city); ONS year ending Dec 2024 (Greater London)
fun_fact: São Paulo's murder rate (4.4) is a quarter of Chicago's (17.5) and about a tenth of Memphis's (40.9). Mexico City (11.0) is lower than Chicago. Caveat: these are official figures from different agencies with different definitions. Chicago PD's own count gives about 21.7, for example. The gaps are large enough that the order holds either way.
headline: City Homicide, Mixed

question: Homicide rate: US cities (FBI). Which is highest?
stat_label: Murder and non-negligent manslaughter per 100,000 residents, 2024 (city police agency)
source_name: FBI Crime Data Explorer, Summary (SRS/NIBRS) agency data, 2024: murder & non-negligent manslaughter
fun_fact: Chicago's reputation is bigger than its murder rate. At 17.5 per 100k it's below Memphis (40.9), Kansas City (27.6) and Washington, DC (25.8), and roughly #35 among US cities of 50,000+. Caveat: these are FBI-reported murders by city police agency. The ranks come from BeautifyData's FBI-based list and are approximate. New Orleans and Jackson, MS didn't report 2024 data, so they aren't ranked.
headline: US City Homicide

question: Who most approves of the switch from communism to a market economy?
stat_label: % who approve of the change to a market economy (Pew Spring 2019, Q16)
source_name: Pew Research Center, "European Public Opinion Three Decades After the Fall of Communism" (Oct 15, 2019), Spring 2019 Global Attitudes Survey
fun_fact: Young Russians (51%) are more pro-market than older Slovaks (49%), even though Slovakia is in the EU and the eurozone. Slovakia has the biggest age gap of any country: 84% of 18–34s approve but only 49% of those 60+. Caveat: about 1,000 people were surveyed per country, so age groups carry roughly ±5–8 pt margins. Russians 18–34 (51) and Slovaks 60+ (49) are statistically tied.
headline: Capitalist Converts

question: Which group of Americans has the most positive view of socialism?
stat_label: % with a very or somewhat positive impression of "socialism" (Pew, Aug 1–14 2022)
source_name: Pew Research Center, "Modest Declines in Positive Views of 'Socialism' and 'Capitalism' in U.S." (Sep 19, 2022), survey of 7,647 adults (ATP Wave 113)
fun_fact: Black (52%) and Asian Americans (49%) view socialism more positively than adults under 30 (44%). Among under-30s, socialism (44%) actually beats capitalism (40%). Caveat: the race and age groups overlap, and the Black (52), Asian (49) and under-30 (44) figures are within each other's margins of error.
headline: Views of Socialism

question: Who eats the most rice per person?
stat_label: Rice available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Bangladesh eats 250.6 kg of rice per person a year, almost twice China's 130.1 kg, and the Philippines (200.4 kg) also out-eats China. Japan is at 72.9 kg (2022 data) and Italy, home of risotto, 9.4 kg. The world #1 is the Gambia (310.7 kg).
headline: Rice Buckets

question: Who eats the most tomatoes per person?
stat_label: Tomatoes available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Turkey eats 112.8 kg of tomatoes per person a year, the most in the world. Mexico, home of salsa, is at only 16.1 kg, far behind the Netherlands (62.0 kg) and China (40.4 kg).
headline: Tomato Towns

question: Who eats the most onions per person?
stat_label: Onions available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Tajikistan leads the world at 56.8 kg of onions per person a year. Senegal (31.1 kg) eats far more than India (17.5 kg), and the US eats 9.6 kg.
headline: Tear Jerkers

question: Which country has the highest suicide rate?
stat_label: Age-standardized suicide rate, both sexes
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator MH_12
fun_fact: Guyana has the world's highest age-standardized suicide rate (54.8 per 100k). Uruguay's (22.2) is the 10th highest, France's (13.9) is above China's (8.0), and Greece's (3.9) is among the lowest in Europe. These are WHO modelled estimates for 2023, with wide uncertainty where death registration is weak.
headline: Global Suicide Rates

question: Which country Googles "anime" the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in the search term "anime"
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, search term, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Mongolia searches "anime" more than anywhere. Japan comes dead last (#82 of 82), because Japanese users search in Japanese (アニメ), not the English word. Caveat: Google Trends measures each country's share of its own Google searches over the past 5 years (scaled so the top country = 100), not search volume or fans. Countries with little Google use are left out. It's a search term, not a topic, so language matters.
headline: Anime Searches

question: Which country Googles Lionel Messi the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in Lionel Messi (person topic)
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, topic entity, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Guinea Googles Lionel Messi more than anywhere. His home country, Argentina, is #7 (43), and Spain, where he made his name at Barcelona, is far lower (10). Caveat: Google Trends measures each country's share of its own Google searches over the past 5 years (scaled so the top country = 100), not search volume or fans. Countries with little Google use are left out.
headline: Messi Fans

question: Who gets the most of its energy from renewables?
stat_label: Renewable energy consumption (% of total final energy consumption)
source_name: World Bank (IEA, IRENA, UN Statistics Division, WHO, World Bank: SDG 7.2 tracking)
fun_fact: Uganda gets 91% of its final energy from renewables, far more than Norway (61%), because firewood and charcoal count as renewable. India (35%) is over three times the US (11%), and Saudi Arabia is near zero. Caveat: 'renewable' includes traditional biomass, so a high share often reflects energy poverty rather than green policy.
headline: Green Machines

question: Which country spends the biggest share of its economy on the military?
stat_label: Military expenditure (% of GDP)
source_name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database via World Bank
fun_fact: Algeria spends 8.8% of its GDP on the military, nearly three times the US share (3.1%), and Poland (4.5%) now outspends the US relative to the size of its economy. China's share is 1.7%. Caveat: this is a share of GDP, not dollars (in dollars the US spends far more than any other country). The figures are SIPRI estimates. Ukraine, #1 at 39.6% while at war, isn't in this set.
headline: Military Share

question: Where do the most adults use tobacco?
stat_label: Prevalence of current tobacco use, smoked or smokeless (% of adults 15+)
source_name: WHO Global Health Observatory via World Bank
fun_fact: France (33.6%) has a higher rate of tobacco use than China (22.8%), and nearly three times the UK's (12.8%). Serbia is #4 in the world at 39.7%. Nigeria is among the lowest at 3.1%. These are WHO estimates for adults 15+, counting any tobacco product but not e-cigarettes.
headline: Smoke Signals

question: Which country is the most forested?
stat_label: Forest area (% of land area)
source_name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment via World Bank
fun_fact: Japan is 68% forest, a bigger share than Brazil (58.5%), home of most of the Amazon, or Canada (42.0%). The UK is just 13.5%. Caveat: this is the share of land, not total forest area. In hectares, Brazil and Canada have far more forest than Japan.
headline: Into the Woods

question: Where is autism most common?
stat_label: Estimated autism cases per 100 people
source_name: IHME Global Burden of Disease 2023 via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Japan's estimated autism rate (1.34 per 100 people) is higher than the US's (0.97) and far above the UK's (0.74). Uganda is #5 in the world. Caveat: these are IHME model estimates built on surveys from relatively few countries. The differences between countries largely reflect how much autism is screened for, diagnosed and reported, not necessarily how common it truly is.
headline: Autism Rates

question: Which country Googles "Minecraft" the most?
stat_label: Google search interest in the search term "Minecraft"
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, search term, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: Myanmar searches "Minecraft" more than anywhere. The Philippines (59) is far ahead of the US (33), and Japan is last of 80 countries (3). Caveat: Google Trends measures each country's share of its own Google searches over the past 5 years (scaled so the top country = 100), not search volume or fans. Countries with little Google use are left out. It's a search term, not a topic, so language matters.
headline: Minecraft Searches

question: Which country sent its first person to space first?
stat_label: Year the country's first citizen flew to space
source_name: Wikipedia: Timeline of space travel by nationality
fun_fact: Vietnam (Phạm Tuân, 1980), Mongolia (1981) and Afghanistan (1988) all had a citizen in space before the UK (Helen Sharman, 1991) and China (Yang Liwei, 2003). Caveat: the first four flew on Soviet Soyuz spacecraft, Vietnam, Mongolia and Afghanistan as guests of the Soviet Interkosmos-era programme; Sharman's flight was a privately funded commercial mission (Project Juno). Only China launched its own astronaut on its own rocket (Shenzhou 5). Nationality is counted at the time of launch, as on Wikipedia's list (e.g. Mongolian People's Republic, Democratic Republic of Afghanistan). Ranks are among the 55 countries on that list.
headline: Space Race

question: Which country has the most serial killers for its size?
stat_label: Known serial killers relative to population
source_name: Aamodt, M.G. (2016). Serial Killer Statistics. Radford University/FGCU Serial Killer Database
fun_fact: Australia (5.23) is #2 of the 21 countries in the database, behind only the US (15.5). Austria (4.03, #6) ranks above Sweden (1.91), Japan (1.19) and Mexico (0.45, #18). The ratio compares a country's share of the database's 4,743 known serial killers with its share of world population (1 = as expected). Caveat: the database has a strong reporting bias. It mostly measures how well killers are caught and documented in English-language sources, not true prevalence.
headline: Known Serial Killers

question: Where is reported erect circumference highest?
stat_label: Average reported erect penis circumference, cm
source_name: World Population Review: Penis Size by Country 2026 (data compiled by Little Big Data)
fun_fact: Taiwan (12.61 cm, #23 of 142) comes out ahead of the US (12.23 cm, #39); Israel (11.70 cm), Vietnam (11.55 cm) and Finland (11.20 cm, #114) trail. France is highest on the source list at 13.63 cm. Caveat: compiled from studies of very different methods and sizes, many self-reported (Taiwan, the US and Israel here), others measured by clinicians (Vietnam, Finland). Self-reports tend to run high, so treat the ranking as rough.
headline: Reported Circumference

question: Where do the most people view Israel unfavorably?
stat_label: % of adults with an unfavorable view of Israel (Pew Research Center, spring 2026)
source_name: Pew Research Center, Spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey (short read, June 4 2026)
fun_fact: Turkey (97%) is #1 of the 36 places surveyed. Japan (83%, #6) is more negative than Germany (73%, #13) and South Korea (70%, tied #15 with Poland). The US (60%, tied #22 with Chile) is among the less negative, though up from 53% in 2025. The median across all 36 is 67% unfavorable, 25% favorable. Caveat: Pew surveyed 44,657 adults in 36 countries and territories (including the West Bank and East Jerusalem; Gaza could not be surveyed) from Feb 8 to May 13 2026; most interviews took place after the US and Israel began a military campaign in Iran on Feb 28. Unfavorable = very plus somewhat unfavorable; people who did not answer are not shown.
headline: Views of Israel

question: Where is the maternal mortality ratio highest?
stat_label: Maternal mortality ratio (deaths per 100,000 live births), 2020
source_name: Wikipedia: List of countries by maternal mortality ratio (WHO Global Health Observatory / UN MMEIG estimates via Our World in Data), 2020 column
fun_fact: The US (21.1 deaths per 100,000 live births, #121 of 185) is higher than Saudi Arabia (16.2, #133) and Moldova (12.3, #139). Japan is at 4.3 (#173), and Belarus has the lowest ratio on the list at 1.1 (#185). The world figure is 223.5. Caveat: these are modelled estimates from the UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, World Bank, UN Population Division). 2020 is the latest column on the Wikipedia list. Countries record maternal deaths differently. In the US, part of the count comes from a pregnancy checkbox on death certificates, which can misclassify some deaths. Small countries with few births can swing a lot from year to year.
headline: Maternal Mortality

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people (UNODC via World Bank, latest year per country, 2021–2023)
source_name: World Bank / UNODC: Intentional homicides (VC.IHR.PSRC.P5)
fun_fact: Costa Rica (17.7), the 'peaceful' tourist favourite, has a far higher homicide rate than Russia (6.8). Lithuania (2.6) is above Canada (2.0) and Sweden (1.1). Caveat: police-recorded homicides; latest year available per country (2018 or later), so years differ.
headline: Recorded Homicides

question: Which country has the highest homicide rate?
stat_label: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people (UNODC via World Bank, latest year per country, 2022–2023)
source_name: World Bank / UNODC: Intentional homicides (VC.IHR.PSRC.P5)
fun_fact: Jamaica (49.4) has one of the highest recorded homicide rates, well above Brazil (19.3). Uruguay (11.2), often seen as South America's safe haven, beats Kenya (4.9); Latvia (2.5) is over four times Italy (0.6). Caveat: police-recorded homicides; latest year available per country (2018 or later).
headline: Homicide Figures

question: Where is the female homicide rate highest?

question: Which US group has the most federal child sex offenders per person?
stat_label: Federal child sex-abuse / child cornography offenders sentenced per million people, by race and ethnicity
source_name: US Sentencing Commission FY2024 individual datafile (USSC FY24) + US Census Bureau population estimates (July 1, 2024)
fun_fact: Per person, non-Hispanic White Americans are the most likely to be sentenced federally for child sex offences (8.8 per million), ahead of Hispanic (6.4) and Black Americans (5.8). Asian and Pacific Islander Americans are lowest (2.7). Offences counted: child cornography (§2G2.2), production of child cornography (§2G2.1), travel for sex with a minor (§2G1.3), statutory rape (§2A3.2) and child exploitation enterprises (§2G2.6); 2,573 people in FY2024. Caveats: these are federal cases only, so most child abuse (prosecuted by states) is missing. Native Americans are left out because federal jurisdiction over reservations inflates their federal counts. Hispanic counts include non-citizens.
headline: Federal Sex Offenders

question: Federal child-sex image offenders per million (FY2023)
stat_label: People sentenced federally for child-sex image offences (§2G2.2) per million residents, by race and ethnicity, FY2023
source_name: US Sentencing Commission, Quick Facts: Child Cornography Offenses (FY2023) + USSC FY2023 datafile (Asian/PI) + US Census Bureau Vintage 2023 national estimates (July 1, 2023)
fun_fact: Per person, White Americans are sentenced federally for child-sex image offences far more often (5.6 per million) than Hispanic (2.8), Black (1.9) or Asian and Pacific Islander Americans (1.7). Method: 1,408 people were sentenced in FY2023; Quick Facts gives 77.1% White, 12.8% Hispanic and 5.8% Black. Each share × 1,408 is divided by the Census July 2023 population (non-Hispanic White, Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black). Quick Facts puts Asian/PI inside “Other races” (4.3%), so the Asian/PI count (36) comes from the USSC FY2023 datafile, which matches Quick Facts for the other groups. Caveat: federal cases only (most child-sex image cases are prosecuted by states), so this reflects federal enforcement as much as offending. Native Americans are left out because federal jurisdiction over reservations inflates their federal counts. USSC “White” and “Black” exclude Hispanic people. This is a narrower measure than the FY2024 “Federal Sex Offenders” puzzle (all federal child sex-abuse guidelines).
headline: Evidence Locker

question: Which US group has the highest suicide rate?

Black men (11.4) and Asian and Pacific Islander men (9.9) are far lower, and White women (7.9) are close to Asian men. Black women have the lowest rate of the six (2.8). Caveat: all race groups are non-Hispanic; rates are age-adjusted to the 2000 US standard population. CDC notes that deaths of American Indian and Alaska Native people are often misclassified to other races on death certificates, so their rate is probably an underestimate. “Asian men” is CDC's non-Hispanic Asian or Pacific Islander group.

question: Who eats the most garlic per person?
